programme.title: The Evolution of American Federalism
programme.sub-title: States Can't Nullify Federal Law
programme.desc: Throughout American history, federal and state governments have clashed over interpretations of the law and states' rights. Survey this rocky relationship across time.

programme.title: The Evolution of American Federalism
programme.sub-title: The Federal Government Can Tax and Spend
programme.desc: Although federal law reigns supreme, the Constitution outlines a limited domain for federal authority. Here, you will learn about the federal power of taxing and spending.

programme.title: The Evolution of American Federalism
programme.sub-title: Guns, the Military, and Foreign Affairs
programme.desc: National defense is a key function of the government, but our Constitution creates a dual system to ensure a balanced federal government. Dive into this system and explore its implications.

programme.title: The Evolution of American Federalism
programme.sub-title: Borders, Immigration, and Citizenship
programme.desc: Shift your attention to immigration, which has been a complex issue for the United States ever since the 18th century. Explore the challenges of borders, immigration laws, and citizenship.

programme.title: The Evolution of American Federalism
programme.sub-title: Commerce Clause: A Source of Federal Power
programme.desc: In this first of two lectures, you will delve into the world of interstate commerce. You will see how the federal power has been curtailed and expanded in different eras.

programme.title: The Evolution of American Federalism
programme.sub-title: Commerce Clause: A Limit on State Power
programme.desc: Continue your study of the Commerce Clause by looking at the boundaries of state authority and the impact on interstate economics. Also examine attempts to regulate internet content.
